text: hey everybody I've been tagged a number of times in a recent video by a Creator who is trying to defend themselves against accusations of being a p3do and
I am not going to share that video or respond to it but I do want to respond to one of the claims that is
foundational to that defense and that is that Creator's claim that they agree with trust and rely on the objective
standard of God's word and there simply is no such thing and I want to talk about three reasons that the Bible does
not present an objective standard the first is that it overwhelmingly conflicts with itself there are very few
issues on which the Bible presents a single a unified a consistent perspective it is the product of
numerous different authors and editors writing and editing over the course of almost a thousand years from different
times from different places from different social social settings two different audiences for different reasons and with different rhetorical
goals and it frequently conflicts with itself so when we try to extract a single objective standard out of the
Bible we are actually going in and negotiating with the different disagreements and deciding which
position we want to prioritize and so we are imposing our needs and our interests and our rhetorical goals on the text
when we presume to identify an objective standard within the Bible overwhelmingly second reason is that on a very
fundamental level the Bible has nothing to say it does not speak it cannot speak because texts have no inherent meaning
it is just a large collection of signs and symbols and the meanings that are associated with those signs and symbols
are based on agreements that people reach and people can have different understandings of those signs and symbols and there can be many different
potential meanings that can be attached to them and so a reading is a process of intuitively generating all the potential
meaning that could be associated with a given linguistic expression and then intuitively whittling it down to what seems most likely and that's important
what seems most likely is going to be governed by the perspectives the experiences the circumstances the
rhetorical needs and goals of the reader because there's no meaning inhabiting any page any screen any signs any sound
waves the meaning is always generated Within Mind of a reader a hearer a viewer their own circumstances are going
to influence how they construct that meaning So reading is always a process of negotiation on a very fundamental
level and that is also not objective even critical Scholars have to try to learn everything they can about the
various different circumstances and contexts and settings that could have generated the text we find in the Bible
so that we can approximate as close as possible a reconstruction of the meaning that was intended by the original
authors and editors but that's never perfect that is always a game of approximation folks who approach the
Bible devotionally confessionally as something authoritative as something inspired are very rarely going to achieve the same degree of approximation
because they're going to be governed more directly by what will make the text more meaningful and more useful to them
and that is going to be influenced by their own circumstances their own needs their own rhetorical goals the third
reason has to do with the fact that the meaning that is generated within the Bible is never static it changes with
Society because the biblical text was not generated and has never functioned independent of society it is embedded
within society and the meanings that people generate are the process of a very complex negotiation between where
Society is going it's social mores it's social standards and the needs and the rhetorical interests and goals of the
people doing the interpreting and here's an illustration of how these three things come together to put the lie to the notion that the Bible has any
objective standard on any issue that is relevant to us today if a man sells his daughter into sex slavery when does she
go free according to Exodus 21 she does not she is a sex slave forever and there
is a rationale behind this it is that she has become betrothed to her master and if she is set free she's no longer
eligible for uh proper Israelite marriage for lack of a better term she
is considered tainted Goods within that ancient society and so she would most likely have to return to live with her
father and be what her father would most likely consider an economic drain on his household now according to Deuteronomy
15 she does go free in the seventh year just like her male counterparts in addition the master must provide her
with provision so that she does not go free empty-handed so this is a way to
allow that freedom while also trying to provide for the person who is going to
struggle to find a place within ancient Israelites Society now what if you don't
think sex slavery is moral what if you think it's sinful well great that's not
biblical there is not a single syllable anywhere in the Bible that categorically condemns slavery or even sex slavery as
immoral as sinful that is the product of that complex negotiation between the
broader social mores and those groups who approach the Bible devotionally and debates about just slavery in general are related to this we had folks from
all sides of this question those who defended slavery those who sought for an incremental removal of slavery those who
were abolitionists those who thought it should just be severely restricted all of them appealed to the Bible as their
Authority for their position when in reality it was society that was changing around them and they were changing with
it and they were using the Bible as their proof text to uphold their specific morality as authorized as
endorsed by God and so the Bible doesn't really change society Society is going to change because it is the interaction
of numerous different people and numerous different circumstances seeking numerous different things the Bible does not operate independent of society it is
not governing Society overwhelmingly Society is governing itself and the Bible is tagging along for the ride
usually as the proof text the authorization for any one of a number of different positions that someone has
arrived at because of society
